To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the maximum transmission of sound pressure waves through a stainless-steel plate occurs when the ratio of thickness of the plate (mm) to the frequency of sound wave (MHz) is an integer multiple of 0.5.
sound pressure is optimally transmitted through stainless steel plates when the thickness of the plates is a multiple of a quarter of the wavelength of the incident sound wave.
sound pressure transmission is optimal when the ratio of plate thickness to the frequency of sound wave is a multiple of a whole number of half wavelengths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a high frequency ultrasound system for the generation of cavitation in a liquid medium, and the optimization of the reactor geometry to maximize the cavitation intensity.
the development of a novel reactor design that can generate a highly localized acoustic field for sonochemistry.

the development of new ultrasound reactor design for sonochemical reactions, where the reactor geometry and the ultrasound frequency can be adjusted to achieve the maximum sound pressure transmission through a metal plate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimal transmission occurs when the plate is thin enough to allow the sound wave to pass through it without significant reflection and thick enough to avoid significant attenuation.
the transmission of ultrasound pressure through a stainless steel plates is maximized at thickness ratios that are a multiple of a quarter of the wavelength of the applied ultrasound.
the transmission of high-frequency ultrasound through stainless steel plates is maximized for thickness ratios of a multiple of half a wavelength of the sound pressure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transmission of high-frequency ultrasound waves through stainless steel plates is highly dependent on the thickness of the steel plate and the frequency of the applied wave.
, in general, the optimal design for a stainless steel plate in a sonochemical reactor should be a plate thickness equal to a multiple of a wavelength of the ultrasound wave.
the optimal thickness of the stainless steel plate to maximize the transmission of high-frequency sound waves is a multiple of a ½ wavelength of the applied sound wave.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of the reactor should be optimized to minimize the attenuation of the ultrasound waves.
the design of stainless steel plate reactors for high frequency ultrasound applications should be optimized to maximize the sound pressure transmission through the reactor walls.
, when designing a reactor for high-frequency sonication, the thickness of the reactor wall should be a multiple of half of the applied sound wave wavelength.
